Article Title: Tesla sees 'Worst Day' since the day Elon Musk said that 'I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames'
Article Text:
Why Elon Musk lost $18.6 billion in a single day

Tesla plans to spend more on AI

Elon Musk avoids merger speculation

Elon Musk’s net worth dropped by $18.6 billion on July 23 after Tesla shares dropped by 14%, marking its largest single-day decline since June 5, 2025. According to Forbes Billionaires List, the drop in Tesla stock lowered Elon Musk’s net worth to $731.7 billion. Despite the fall, he remains the world’s richest person ahead of Google co-founder Larry Page ($263.8 billion) and Amazon’s Jeff Bezos ($245.4 billion). The drop comes days after Musk said “I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames.” He was then talking about the widespread protests at Tesla showrooms and vandalism of the vehicles.Tesla shares plunged after the company reported quarterly results that missed profit expectations despite beating revenue estimates. The car maker posted revenue of $28.2 billion, above analysts' estimate of $27.2 billion, according to FactSet. However, earnings came in at 33 cents per share, well below the expected 55 cents per share.As per a Forbes article, the weak profit numbers, combined with Tesla's plans to continue spending heavily on AI, weighed on investor sentiment.During the earnings call, Tesla Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said the company still expects to spend $25 billion this year, with even higher investments planned in the coming years.The spending is aimed at supporting Tesla's AI ambitions, including its Optimus humanoid robot and robotaxi business.However, analysts said investors now want to see clear progress rather than promises.Morgan Stanley analysts said the spending is a "necessary investment" but added that Tesla must deliver "tangible" milestones for its robotaxi and Optimus projects.Canaccord Genuity analysts also said they expect meaningful robotaxi deployments over the next six months as Tesla expands its AI strategy.During the earnings call, Elon Musk was also asked about speculation surrounding a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX. The tech billionaire declined to comment on combining the two companies, saying such discussions cannot happen during an earnings call. However, Musk acknowledged there is "more and more overlap" between the businesses, pointing to Starlink connectivity in Cybertrucks and the proposed TeraFab AI chip manufacturing venture involving Tesla and SpaceX.
Article Summary: Elon Musk’s net worth dropped by $18.6 billion on July 23 after Tesla shares dropped by 14%, marking its largest single-day decline since June 5, 2025. According to Forbes Billionaires List, the drop in Tesla stock lowered Elon Musk's net worth to $731.7 billion. The drop comes days after Musk said “I can’t pass a TV without spotting a Tesla up in flames”

Article Title: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is hiring software engineers, designers, researchers for his 'tech crew': Here's what the job actually is
Article Text:
NYC mayor wants his ‘tech crew’ to build city software from inside the agency



New York City is betting that in-house tech teams will ship faster and cost less



New York City has opened applications for a new kind of government job. Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Monday that the city is recruiting software engineers, product designers, product managers, user researchers, service designers and data experts to staff what he is calling Public Interest Technology Crews—PIT Crews, a pun the mayor committed to by rolling up to the Coney Island go-kart track to make the announcement.The hiring is funded and specific. A City Hall spokesperson confirmed around 30 full-time roles across four crews, supported by $5.24 million in baseline funding in the mayor's new fiscal budget. The listings are live at nyc.gov/pitcrew.A PIT Crew is a mixed team—engineers, designers, product managers, user researchers and data experts—placed alongside staff at a city agency rather than parked in a separate technology department. The crew works with that agency and with New Yorkers to design, build and launch a digital tool, then learn from how people actually use it. The mayor's office describes the timeline as months rather than years, which is the entire premise of the model.Five crews are planned. One handles the Click to Cancel complaint portal, three are attached to Mamdani's affordability and public excellence agenda, and a fifth is being developed with support from The Rockefeller Foundation through the Mayor's Fund to Advance New York City.Zohran Mamdani’s PIT crew’s first assignment is a complaint portal with teethCrew one works with the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection on an online portal where New Yorkers can report companies that make subscriptions near-impossible to cancel. It supports the Click to Cancel rule Mamdani announced last week, which requires businesses to offer the same exit route customers used to sign up. Enforcement begins October 1, and the junk fees ban lands January 1, 2027.The portal is built to do two things at once—give individual New Yorkers a route to recourse, and give City Hall a running database of repeat offenders.Chief Technology Officer and OTI Commissioner Lisa Gelobter framed the roles around a shift in what government technology now is. Every service has a digital surface, she argued, and every confusing step in that surface erodes trust. Her operating instruction for the crews is user first, always, with outcomes weighted over outputs.There is a politics to the hiring as well. NYC-DSA's Tech Action organisers backed the announcement as a choice to build capacity inside government rather than route taxpayer money to consultancies and big tech vendors. BetaNYC's Noel Hidalgo made the cost version of the same argument—in-house teams that deliver faster and cheaper than the outsourced alternative."New Yorkers should not be forced to navigate systems that are confusing, outdated and burdened by bureaucracy," Mamdani said. "The PIT Crew turns that model on its head."Public Interest Technology took shape as a field in the 2010s on a fairly unglamorous premise: government software is usually bad, and fixing it is a staffing and usability problem more than an engineering one. The recruitment page leans into that, pitching the work rather than the salary—the goal, it says, is to make interacting with government dignified and delightful for every New Yorker.
Article Summary: New York City launches Public Interest Technology Crews (PIT Crews) Crews will build city software from inside the agency rather than in a separate department. Hiring is funded by $5.24 million in the mayor's new fiscal budget.

Article Title: NASA has grown plants in space for years: New research says the next step is growing medicines, starting with a tobacco and a virus
Article Text:
How UC San Diego grew cowpea mosaic virus on tobacco and black-eyed pea plants in simulated microgravity

Blood clots, cut-short missions and why medical emergencies on the ISS make Mars pharmaceuticals urgent

Astronauts heading to Mars will be gone for roughly 400 days, and everything they need has to travel with them or arrive ahead of them. Food is the problem everyone talks about. The bigger one might be the medicine cabinet. More than half the pharmaceuticals stocked on the International Space Station expire within three years—well short of the window a Mars crew would need them for. Expired drugs aren't just weaker. They can turn toxic.A new study out of the University of California San Diego proposes a workaround that sounds almost absurdly simple: grow the medicine on the way. Researchers cultivated a plant virus with therapeutic properties in a lab setup engineered to mimic microgravity, and the results suggest astronauts could one day farm their own pharmaceuticals mid-flight instead of watching a supply cabinet slowly go bad.The virus in question is cowpea mosaic virus, or CPMV, which has shown promise in prompting the human immune system to attack cancer cells. The UC San Diego team grew it on two hosts—Nicotiana benthamiana, a cousin of the tobacco plant, and Vigna unguiculata no. 5, better known as the black-eyed pea. The pea plant is the interesting one. It grows the virus and produces edible food, which makes it a two-for-one on a spacecraft where every square centimetre is contested.To simulate weightlessness, the plants sat on a random positioning machine that tumbled in three dimensions, driven by a custom Python script running on a Raspberry Pi. Harvesting was the clever part. Instead of destroying the plant, engineers pulled apoplastic fluid from the leaves using a vacuum, then spun it in a centrifuge to isolate the viral extract. The ISS already has a lab-grade centrifuge on board.They have already happened. A NASA astronaut was found to have a blood clot during a routine ultrasound in 2018 and was put on enoxaparin to prevent a pulmonary embolism. More recently, astronaut Mike Fincke's medical emergency cut his ISS mission short. Motion sickness, headaches, and urinary tract infections are routine. On Mars, there is no early return flight—only what the crew can grow.
Article Summary: UC San Diego grew cowpea mosaic virus on tobacco and black-eyed pea plants in simulated microgravity. The results suggest astronauts could one day farm their own pharmaceuticals mid-flight. More than half the pharmaceuticals stocked on the International Space Station expire within three years.

Article Title: ‘AI ending humanity is complete nonsense’: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang challenges fellow tech CEOs on doomsday scenario
Article Text:
Jensen Huang (File Image)

Silicon Valley divided over existential risk



Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued a rebuke against widespread ‘AI doomsday’ warnings, dismissing catastrophic claims that artificial intelligence (AI) will destroy civilization or trigger mass unemployment. In an interview with Axios, Huang warned that scaring workers, businesses and lawmakers away from adopting AI poses a far greater economic danger than the technology itself.“The fact that this is going to be the end of humanity — it's complete nonsense. The fact that this is going to destroy half of the American jobs is complete nonsense,” Huang was quoted as saying.Huang’s comments stand in stark contrast to warnings issued by other prominent AI leaders and industry pioneers. Previously, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated AI could “most likely lead to the end of the world” and co-signed a public declaration urging global leaders to treat AI extinction risks with urgency.Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has been most vocal about the negative effects of the technology. He has repeatedly cautioned that rapid AI training trajectories could lead to massive job displacement and potentially catastrophic outcomes for humanity.Elon Musk has also been warning of severe societal risks and calling for pauses on unchecked AI deployment.Huang’s intervention arrives as Washington aims to balance two major AI policy challenges: establishing domestic guardrails for powerful models while preventing overly restrictive rules that could handicap US tech giants.Huang argues that overreacting to hypothetical extinction scenarios risks suffocating practical innovation across medical diagnostics, scientific research and enterprise automation. He said that instead of restricting technology out of fear, America must push forward aggressively to maintain its competitive edge on the global stage.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang dismisses claims that artificial intelligence will destroy civilization or trigger mass unemployment. He argues that scaring workers, businesses and lawmakers away from adopting AI poses a far greater economic danger than the technology itself. His comments stand in stark contrast to warnings issued by other prominent AI leaders and industry pioneers.

Article Title: IIRIS Consulting acquires publicly-listed fintech company Dion Global Solutions
Article Text: IIRIS Consulting (Indus IntelliRisk and IntelliSense Services Private Limited) has acquired Dion Global Solutions Limited, a publicly listed fintech company. The acquisition follows the approval of IIRIS's resolution plan by the National Company Law Tribunal on 21 July 2026.The acquisition marks IIRIS's entry into the listed company space and gives its IntelliFuture suite of AI-enabled products an immediate route to market. Dion's customer base includes HDFC Bank , Canara Bank, Sharekhan, JM Financial, Indiabulls Ventures, IIFL, Jhaveri Securities, Equitas Small Finance Bank and BgSE Financials Limited.Under the terms of the resolution plan, which carries a total value of Rs 802.93 lakh, IIRIS has infused fresh capital into Dion Global through the subscription of 50,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each. The acquisition gives IIRIS a listed platform and an installed base across India’s banking and capital markets ecosystem, and the firm intends to invest further in Dion’s technology, people and product roadmap as the combined business scales.Garry Singh, President, IIRIS Consulting, said, “Every conversation we have with a bank, a broker or a wealth manager today is about digitisation. Institutions want risk, compliance and case management to run on technology rather than on paper, and IIRIS made a deliberate decision to build for that shift.This acquisition positions us exactly where the market is heading. We move from being a risk firm that built technology to a technology company with three decades of financial markets infrastructure under its roof. ”At the centre of the combined offering is the IntelliFuture suite, a family of seven AI-enabled products built from IIRIS’s investigation and risk experience.Sagarika Chakraborty, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, IIRIS Consulting, said, “IIRIS built its name on investigations, forensic intelligence and risk advisory delivered as a service, and we converted that experience into the IntelliFuture suite of AI-enabled products covering fraud classification, case tracking, asset tracing and risk visibility. Dion completes the picture. Its platforms already sit inside more than 250 banks, brokers and wealth managers, which means the intelligence we once delivered as reports can now live as a capability inside our clients' own systems. Our immediate focus is a seamless transition for Dion's clients and employees.”IIRIS also brings an international footprint, with offices and products deployed across Middle East, Europe and Asia.
Article Summary: IIRIS has infused fresh capital into Dion Global through the subscription of 50,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each. The acquisition gives IIRIS a listed platform and an installed base across India’s banking and capital markets ecosystem.

Article Title: Swiggy, Zepto, Meesho deposit Karnataka gig welfare fee
Article Text: Eternal, Zepto, Swiggy, Urban Company and Meesho have deposited the welfare fee mandated under Karnataka’s gig-worker law, even as the companies continue to challenge the legislation in the high court.The platforms deposited the money following a Karnataka High Court direction, industry body Internet and Mobile Association of India said on Thursday. It did not disclose the amount paid by the companies.The law seeks to create a state-run fund for the social security and welfare of people working through delivery, ride-hailing, home-service and other digital platforms. It also introduces worker registration, grievance-redressal and transparency requirements for platforms.Earlier this month, the high court declined to stay the law but protected the companies from coercive action for the time being. It asked them to deposit their disputed second-quarter welfare contributions with the court. The money will remain separate until the case is decided.The platforms have argued that Karnataka’s requirements overlap with the Centre’s Code on Social Security and could result in companies paying twice towards gig-worker welfare.The state government has maintained that the two laws do not conflict.IAMAI said the companies were seeking “harmonisation” between the central and state frameworks to avoid duplication and ensure that “every rupee contributed translates into maximum benefit for gig workers.”The platforms said they already fund accident and health insurance, maternity assistance, emergency support and programmes that help workers access credit. Collectively, their initiatives cover a broader pool of more than six million monthly active platform workers across India, according to IAMAI.Meesho, which was separately questioned about the law during its June-quarter analyst call, said it had already accounted for the potential financial impact. “From a conservative standpoint, we continue to make provisions and provide for any of those costs into our P&L,” Meesho management said. This means its reported expenses already factor in the possibility that it may eventually have to bear the fee.“There shouldn’t be any adverse impact if we are required to pay it,” management said, adding that the amounts involved were “not material in nature.”Under the state’s current fee structure, platforms must contribute 50 paise for a delivery made using a two-wheeler, 75 paise for a three-wheeler and Re 1 for a four-wheeler, the Karnataka government told the court. The case is scheduled to be heard again on July 31.
Article Summary: Eternal, Zepto, Swiggy, Urban Company and Meesho have deposited the welfare fee mandated under Karnataka’s gig-worker law. The companies continue to challenge the legislation in the high court. The law seeks to create a state-run fund for the social security and welfare of people working through delivery, ride- hailing, home-service and other digital platforms.

Article Title: Swiggy board clears 49.5% foreign ownership cap
Article Text: Swiggy’s board on Thursday approved a proposal to cap foreign ownership in the company at 49.5%, making its most concrete move yet toward becoming an Indian-owned and controlled company.The proposal will go to shareholders at Swiggy’s annual general meeting on August 18. It will need approval through a special resolution.The cap will apply to total foreign ownership on a fully diluted basis. This includes foreign portfolio investors, non-resident Indians, and Indian companies or investment vehicles that are themselves foreign-owned or controlled.The move comes weeks after Swiggy told stock exchanges that foreign investment in the company stood at 49.76% as of July 6. At the time, the company said the number did not, by itself, change its ownership, control, management, voting rights or shareholder rights.That earlier disclosure was only a snapshot. In a listed company, foreign ownership can move up or down as shares trade. The latest proposal is different. If shareholders approve it, Swiggy will have a formal guardrail to stop foreign ownership from moving beyond 49.5%.The company is also seeking changes to its Articles of Association.Swiggy said these changes are part of its broader effort to qualify as an Indian-owned and controlled company under foreign exchange laws. The proposed changes include removing some existing individual and institutional nomination rights and revising nomination rights for specified resident individuals.This is important because Indian-owned and controlled status depends on two things: who owns the company and who controls it. Ownership is linked to shareholding. Control can also depend on board seats, nomination rights, voting rights and shareholder agreements.For Swiggy, the larger issue is quick commerce. India’s foreign investment rules allow foreign-funded e-commerce companies to run marketplaces. But they restrict inventory-led e-commerce, where the platform owns goods and sells them directly to customers.This does not mean Swiggy immediately plans to move Instamart to an inventory-led model. The company has not said so. But an Indian-owned and controlled structure could give the group more flexibility over how it organises sourcing, inventory and investments across subsidiaries.Swiggy’s move follows a similar step by Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit. Eternal shareholders last year approved a 49.5% foreign ownership cap to preserve its domestic status. A Nishith Desai Associates note said the move was aimed at keeping flexibility for Blinkit and avoiding the risk of Zomato’s investment into Blinkit being treated as indirect foreign investment.
Article Summary: The proposal will go to shareholders at Swiggy’s annual general meeting on August 18. It will need approval through a special resolution. This includes foreign portfolio investors, non-resident Indians, and Indian companies or investment vehicles that are themselves foreign-owned or controlled.

Article Title: This 16-year-old Canadian student built an AI robot turtle that hunts plastic invisible to the eye, and won $50,000 for it
Article Text:
Evan Budz, 16, with the autonomous bionic sea turtle robot that uses AI and an underwater holographic camera to detect microplastics in lakes — the project that won him a $50,000 scholarship at the 2026 Regeneron ISEF.

Robot turtle inspired by a snapping turtle on an Ontario camping trip

AI microplastic detection at 10 microns: how the holographic camera works

Why microplastic lab testing is slow and expensive, and what this robot changes

A 16-year-old student from Ontario, Canada has built a robotic sea turtle that swims on its own, dives to a set depth, and uses AI to spot microplastics floating in lakes and oceans. Evan Budz won a $50,000 scholarship for the project at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in May, taking home the Gordon E. Moore Award for Positive Outcomes for Future Generations.The machine did not start out impressive. Budz's first prototype went straight to the bottom of his grandparents' backyard pool in Canada. He described it sinking like a brick, unable to swim or hold its depth. That was the summer of 2024, and it took roughly 2,000 hours of building to get the robot working, plus another 2,000 on the underwater holographic camera mounted on its shell.The idea came from a snapping turtle Budz watched while camping with his family earlier that year. He was struck by how fluid the movement was, and decided to build something that copied it. Turtles turned out to be a practical choice beyond the aesthetics.They are efficient swimmers, which matters for long missions where recharging is not an option. They are also large enough to carry sensors and imaging gear inside the shell, and common enough across aquatic environments that other organisms are not spooked by them.To get the motion right, Budz studied research literature and video, then consulted staff at Ripley's Aquarium about how green sea turtle flippers actually generate thrust. The flippers were designed in CAD, 3D-printed, and driven by a custom multi-axis servo mechanism that changes the angle of attack between upstroke and downstroke. Computational fluid dynamics simulations refined the shape before any of it hit the water. A spherical dome on the front of the chassis cut drag by 65% compared with a flat endcap.Depth control runs on a variable ballast system built from a linear servo and two syringes, with a pressure sensor feeding a PID loop. In testing between 20 and 150 cm, it held its target depth within 5 cm. A 9-axis inertial measurement unit handles heading, and the robot completed three-pass and four-pass grid searches in a 4x5 m pool with tracking error under 5 degrees.The detection side is where the AI comes in. Budz started building the holographic imaging system in the summer of 2025, and the hard part was tuning the hardware to resolve particles as small as 10 microns and tell plastic apart from small organisms. By the time ISEF came around, the system was hitting 94% accuracy on that distinction.Budz calls the standard process convoluted. Samples go to a laboratory, analysis takes days even for small batches, and it costs money. None of that works in a remote lake with no lab and no trained technicians nearby. His robot analyses the water where it swims.The Ocean Conservancy estimates 11 million metric tons of plastic waste reach the ocean every year, affecting more than 1,300 marine species. Over 1,700 students competed at this year's ISEF, which handed out more than $7 million in total. Budz plans to put the scholarship toward a university degree in science or engineering.
Article Summary: Evan Budz, 16, from Ontario, Canada has built a robotic sea turtle that swims on its own, dives to a set depth, and uses AI to spot microplastics floating in lakes and oceans. He won a $50,000 scholarship for the project at the 2026 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair.

Article Title: After accusing Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI of ‘stealing’ Anthropic's Fable model, Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of ‘Entity List designations’
Article Text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of Entity List designation

‘Moonshot AI used Nvidia chips to train models’



Read full post by Michael Kratsios on X



We have information that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic’s Fable for the development of its K3 model.

To do this they developed a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large scale distillation against U.S. models, allowing them to quickly switch between multiple methods of access to avoid detection. Moonshot AI has also acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.

The United States strongly supports the free and fair development of AI, including a thriving competitive ecosystem that spans frontier models, specialized systems, open-source frameworks, and open-weight models. Legitimate AI distillation used to create smaller, more efficient models plays a vital role in this open innovation ecosystem. However, large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI and other Chinese AI companies of ‘Entity List’ designations after accusing them of using outputs from American frontier models, and saying that the officials have identified ‘evidence of US Al models appearing in some Chinese systems’.“We support open-source AI and the innovation it unlocks. But open source is not open season on American IP. When PRC firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table,” Bessent said in a post on X.US Entity List is a trade restriction tool that consists of groups that the US thinks are acting against the country’s national security. It also restricts sensitive technology exports and requires special government licenses.Bessent’s comments came soon after a senior White House official has accused Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup Moonshot AI of illegally tapping into restricted Nvidia chips to train its new AI model that the company claimed is as powerful as Anthropic’s Fable 5. The allegations follow Moonshot’s release of Kimi K3, a massive open-source model with 2.8 trillion parameters.The model has sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley after closing the performance gap with top American AI systems.Michael Kratsios, Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, publicly raised the alarm, accusing the Chinese company of circumventing strict US export controls to access Nvidia's high-end hardware abroad.Under current US trade restrictions, Nvidia’s most advanced AI semiconductors are strictly banned from being exported to China. While the US has permitted the use and sale of lower-powered chips, the high-performance Nvidia GB300 systems fall under tight restrictions due to their importance in training large-scale neural networks.
Article Summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warns Chinese companies of ‘Entity List’ designations. US officials have identified ‘evidence of US Al models appearing in some Chinese systems’ Moonshot AI has also acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its models.

Article Title: Meesho bets lower prices will power growth as delivery costs fall
Article Text: Meesho expects products on its marketplace to become more affordable as it cuts delivery costs and passes most of those savings to sellers and shoppers, even as higher fuel prices and wages push up expenses across the ecommerce industry.The value-focused ecommerce platform said its cost per delivered order fell by about Re 1 sequentially in the June quarter. This was despite an increase in fuel costs and minimum wages in some states.“You should anticipate that we will continue to reduce our logistics cost at a very good pace,” founder and CEO Vidit Aatrey told analysts on Thursday. “Changes in fuel prices as well as minimum wages are going to be small blips in that entire picture.”Meesho’s average order value declined about 2% from a year earlier. The company said this was a smaller fall than usual because higher raw-material and delivery costs temporarily lifted prices. Over time, it expects average order values to decline by roughly 5% annually as efficiencies make lower-priced transactions viable.“As we start gaining more efficiencies and passing some of those on to customers, we will resume on the trajectory of average order values becoming lower,” CFO Dhiresh Bansal added.The strategy is central to Meesho’s pitch to value-conscious consumers, many of whom are first-time or relatively new online shoppers. The company competes with larger ecommerce platforms that have also sharpened their focus on goods priced below Rs 1,000.Aatrey said the competitive environment had always been intense and had not changed materially after recent moves by rivals. “People have launched sub-platforms to compete with us over the last many years,” he said. “Our pricing is getting better, our selection is getting better, and we continue to see good growth as well as cohort retention.”Meesho’s revenues rose 45% to Rs 3,826 crore in the June quarter, while its losses narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore. Net merchandise value, or the value of goods sold after cancellations and returns, increased 34% to Rs 11,614 crore.The Bengaluru-based company had 274 million annual transacting users, up 29% from a year earlier. Orders placed during the quarter also rose 29% to 725 million.Valmo, Meesho’s logistics network, continued to handle roughly half of its shipments. The company said it allocates deliveries lane by lane to whichever partner offers the lowest cost, rather than trying to raise Valmo’s share for its own sake.“The ultimate share of Valmo would depend on all of these factors,” Bansal said. “The direction of the cost per delivered order would continue to come down. That is the objective with which we work.”The company plans to retain gains from advertising as profit, while passing a large part of future logistics savings back through lower prices. About two-thirds of sellers contributing to Meesho’s merchandise value already advertise on the platform. Management expects this share to increase as more sellers compete for visibility.Meesho maintained its longer-term expectation of about 25% annual growth in merchandise value over five years. It said growth would likely be faster in the initial years and moderate later.
Article Summary: Meesho expects products on its marketplace to become more affordable as it cuts delivery costs. The value-focused ecommerce platform said its cost per delivered order fell by about Re 1 sequentially. This was despite an increase in fuel costs and minimum wages in some states.

Article Title: In 1960, IMAX technology changed cinema; now Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey can be seen in true 70mm format at only 41 theatres worldwide because of this 50-year-old 'machine problem'
Article Text:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is available in limited 70mm IMAX theaters worldwide. This scarcity stems from aging technology and the lack of new projector manufacturing. IMAX must rebuild and retrofit its old machines, which are large and complex. The film prints themselves are also massive, weighing hundreds of pounds. This combination restricts screenings to only forty-one global locations.

The

Odyssey

Variety

“There’s certainly more demand. The problem is they haven’t made new IMAX film projectors in about 50 years. So we retrofit them [and] rebuild them, and part of our strategy is to see how far we can take it.”

The Odyssey

A technology that dates back to the 1960s

Why replacing these projectors isn't easy

“Simply put, a 15/70mm projector isn’t just another mechanical assembly you can spin up on a modern production line in a factory somewhere. It’s a bespoke engineering solution to a bespoke physical problem, and that solution was designed for, and built in, a manufacturing era that ended decades ago.”

The film reels are equally demanding

The Odyssey

The Odyssey

Christopher Nolan'sis playing in IMAX cinemas worldwide, but viewers wanting to watch the film in its intended 70mm IMAX format have only 41 theatres to choose from. The reason is not limited demand or a marketing strategy, but a decades-old technology challenge: IMAX has not manufactured new 70mm film projectors for around 50 years, leaving the company to rebuild and retrofit ageing machines.Explaining the shortage, IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond recently toldThe scarcity means only a small number of theatres globally can screenin true 70mm IMAX format.IMAX is often associated with modern blockbusters, but the technology was developed in the late 1960s. Most cinemas have gone digital over the years, and the number of venues that could show large-format 70mm IMAX film has slowly dwindled.Today, most IMAX theatres use dual 2K digital projectors with a 1.90:1 aspect ratio, which are comparatively easier to manufacture and maintain. By contrast, 15/70mm IMAX projectors are specialised mechanical systems built for large-format film and require dedicated infrastructure to operate.The machines themselves are considerably larger than conventional film projectors, standing over 5.5 feet tall and nearly 6.5 feet long, weighing around two tons. They also use high-powered xenon lamps that require separate cooling systems.Unlike digital projection systems, 70mm IMAX projectors are no longer manufactured at scale. As the film industry transitioned to digital formats, many of the companies that produced components and the expertise required to maintain them also disappeared.Describing the challenge, Redshark News wrote,As a result, IMAX now refurbishes and upgrades existing projectors instead of building new ones.The equipment is only one part of the challenge. A feature-length 70mm IMAX print is significantly larger than conventional film reels. Individual sections are shipped separately to cinemas before being hand-spliced together over several hours into a single reel.A 2.5-hour IMAX film print stretches nearly 10 miles, weighs about 550 pounds and costs approximately $36,000 to produce. Sinceruns for nearly three hours, its print is even longer.Any failure in the projection system can be difficult to repair because replacement parts and technicians familiar with the equipment are limited. This combination of ageing machinery, specialised engineering and declining manufacturing capacity has left only 41 theatres worldwide capable of presentingin its intended 70mm IMAX format.
Article Summary: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is only available in 41 theatres worldwide. This is due to a lack of new projector manufacturing. IMAX must rebuild and retrofit its old machines, which are large and complex. The film prints themselves are also massive, weighing hundreds of pounds.

Article Title: First time in 22 years, Google burns through $6 billion in cash; and CFO Anat Ashkenazi has further 'warning' on cash flow remaining under pressure

Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai

Alphabet CFO issues cash flow warning as AI CapEx soars



‘Full-steam ahead for Gemini 4’: Pichai



For the first time since going public over two decades ago, Google burned through cash in the second quarter. The shift underscores the tech giant’s massive push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Alphabet reported that its free cash flow for the three months ending in June plunged to minus $5.9 billion, falling far below Wall Street expectations. The cash deficit was driven by another major hike in its budget for data centres, custom chips and specialised AI hardware.Google CFO Anat Ashkenazi raised the company’s 2026 capital expenditure (CapEx) forecast to $195 billion to $205 billion – up from earlier guidance of $180 billion to $190 billion. Ashkenazi warned investors that cash reserves will remain squeezed as the company continues to spend aggressively to capture market share.“We expect that free cash flow will remain under pressure driven by our investments in technical infrastructure, which enable us to capitalise on the AI opportunity and continue to drive attractive returns,” Ashkenazi stated during the earnings call.Google is locked in an AI arms race alongside rivals Microsoft, Meta and Amazon.Combined, the four tech giants are on track to spend over $725 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026 alone, reports have said. To fund this massive buildout, Alphabet has taken on nearly $100 billion in debt and raised roughly $85 billion in its first share sale in over twenty years.Google CEO Sundar Pichai reaffirmed the company’s commitment to leading the global AI landscape, telling investors that Google is allocating massive computing power toward training its next flagship frontier model, Gemini 4.“It feels like we are in very early innings of what feels like a secular shift across multiple areas. Over the past year, we’ve gotten more bullish on the opportunities ahead,” Pichai told investors. Google also said that there’s a commercial cloud backlog climbing to $514 billion, maintaining that the cash burn is a necessary trade-off to secure a dominant position in the evolving AI era.

Article Title: Xbox's new PC emulator isn't emulating the original Xbox. It's emulating an Xbox 360.
Article Text:
Xbox's new PC emulator is quietly running Xbox 360 code.

What Project Helix has to do with any of this

Microsoft turned on Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC on July 22 with four original Xbox games—BLiNX: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge and Fuzion Frenzy. They run natively on Windows and handhelds for the first time in 25 years, sold through the Xbox PC app or included with any Game Pass plan. Existing digital console licences carry over.Engineers examining the release files on ResetERA found XEX2 and STFS signatures, plus a kernel string reading "XENON KERNEL EXITING"—markers of Microsoft's Xbox 360 Xenon Fusion emulator. So the setup is layered: an emulated Xbox 360 running the 360's own original-Xbox compatibility mode. It's a roundabout route, but it means the harder engineering problem—emulating 360 architecture on x86—has already shipped.Xbox's next console, Project Helix, will run a version of Windows and play PC games. Moving the back catalogue onto PC now gives that machine a library on day one. "This marks the beginning of a broader effort to preserve XBOX games from the past and bring them to PC over time," wrote Jason Ronald, VP of next generation at Xbox.The context isn't flattering. PlayStation stops producing physical software in January 2028. The Video Game History Foundation estimates around 90 percent of games released are no longer legally purchasable. And Microsoft is in its fifth round of layoffs since the Activision Blizzard merger, cutting 3,200 roles from its games division this fiscal year—one commenter on the announcement noted the person running the console back-compat programme was among the 1,600 let go earlier in July.The four titles do get genuine additions: 4x upscaling on the original 480p output, VSync, anisotropic filtering, enhanced anti-aliasing, windowed and fullscreen modes, and achievements in the coming months. Minimum spec is Windows 11, 8GB RAM, and a GTX 950 or Intel Arc A310.Microsoft has said nothing about the Xbox 360 library. The emulator says it's possible.
Article Summary: Microsoft turned on Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC on July 22. Four original Xbox games run natively on Windows and handhelds for the first time in 25 years. Existing digital console licences carry over. Microsoft is in its fifth round of layoffs since the Activision Blizzard merger.

Article Title: Apple can shut down your 'rented' iPhone if you miss a payment
Article Text:
Miss a payment on a leased iPhone and iOS 27's "Restricted Mode" could leave you with nine apps—nearly all of them built to help you pay up.

Apple's new Restricted Mode leaves you just enough phone to settle the bill

Apple starts renting out iPhones on July 28

Miss a payment on your leased iPhone and Apple may switch most of it off. Code buried in the iOS 27 beta describes a system that lets a financing partner push a device into "Restricted Mode," locking out nearly every app until the account is back in good standing. The finding, first reported by 9to5Mac and picked up by The Verge, lands days before Apple is expected to open sign-ups for its new Apple Upgrade leasing program.The framework is called App Managed Features. An authorised finance app enrols the iPhone, then keeps checking whether the contract is current. If it isn't, the lockdown kicks in and only a short allowlist survives—Phone, Wallet, App Store, Settings, Passwords, Clock, Health, Magnifier and Accessibility Reader. Read that list again and the logic is obvious. Wallet updates your card, Phone calls the lender, Passwords fixes a login problem. Nearly everything left standing exists so you can pay.There's no fixed number of missed payments that triggers it. That call belongs to the financing partner's app, which sets its own policy. Apps that send critical alerts—Messages, Home, some medication and safety apps—may stay reachable, though the provider appears to have a say there too.One gap worth noting: the code doesn't touch App Store subscriptions, so a service could keep billing you while its app sits behind the wall.Apple has also built a matching activation lock, called Partner Finance Lock, that stops a restricted device from being erased, resold or broken down for parts. It lives inside Find My so it survives a restore. The lender doesn't get location data from it.Apple Upgrade, as Bloomberg reports, opens July 28 in the US with Klarna financing it. Leases run 24 months on iPhone and Apple Watch, 36 on Mac and iPad, and signing up needs only a soft credit check. Pay it off early, upgrade mid-term or keep the thing at the end—all allowed, some of it for a fee. AppleCare doesn't come bundled, which the old iPhone Upgrade Program did include. The cheap stuff is out too: Apple Watch SE, base iPad, iPhone 16 and the MacBook Neo don't qualify.Why now isn't much of a mystery. Apple pushed Mac and iPad prices up by hundreds of dollars last month, pinning it on the memory shortage the AI data-centre build-out has turned ugly. The iPhone dodged that round and probably won't dodge September. A monthly plan softens the sticker, and Klarna absorbs the defaults—the same problem that soured Goldman Sachs on Apple Card. All of this sits in a beta, so the restriction code may still change or vanish. Apple hasn't commented.
Article Summary: Apple's new Restricted Mode leaves you just enough phone to settle the bill. An authorised finance app enrols the iPhone, then keeps checking whether the contract is current. If it isn't, the lockdown kicks in and only a short allowlist survives. Apple starts renting out iPhones on July 28.

Article Title: Denis Machuel, CEO of Europe's largest staffing company Adecco says: AI will not wipe out millions of jobs, here's what evidence points to based on data we have so far
Article Text:
Representative Image

“AI is bringing a massive evolution in the world of work, but a job apocalypse is not on the horizon. It's more about changing roles and tasks than eliminating jobs."

Employment data does not indicate mass job losses

"With the data we have so far, there's no evidence we will have a different scenario with AI,"

AI cited in layoffs, but other factors also at play

Entry-level roles are changing

Artificial intelligence is changing how companies work, but it is not triggering a collapse in employment, according to Denis Machuel, CEO of staffing company Adecco Group. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, the chief executive of Europe's largest HR and staffing company cited employment data collected since the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT and said that there is currently no evidence that AI is causing the large-scale job losses many have feared.Speaking to Reuters, Machuel said,He added that, based on available data, AI appears to be reshaping jobs rather than removing them altogether.The findings come from an Adecco study released this week, which examined labour market trends more than three years after ChatGPT's launch. The company cited data from the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), covering its 38 member countries, showing employment rates remain at record highs. At the same time, unemployment is close to historic lows.Machuel said previous technological shifts, including the adoption of steam power, electricity, information technology and the internet, transformed the nature of work without leading to widespread, permanent job destruction.he told Reuters.The comments come as several companies continue restructuring while increasing investment in artificial intelligence. Microsoft recently announced it would cut about 2.1% of its workforce, joining companies including HSBC, Amazon and Standard Chartered in reducing jobs while allocating more resources to AI initiatives.According to global outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, employers have attributed nearly a quarter of job cuts in the United States this year to AI.However, Machuel told Reuters that some companies were using AI to justify layoffs that were actually driven by weaker business performance, restructuring efforts, or other operational challenges.Machuel acknowledged that some entry-level positions are disappearing as AI automates certain tasks. However, he said organisations cannot continue eliminating junior roles without affecting their long-term talent pipeline.Instead, he said companies should redesign these positions so AI complements employees rather than replacing them. He also stressed the need for upskilling and reskilling workers, alongside closer collaboration between businesses, governments and education systems to prepare employees for changing workplace requirements.
Article Summary: Denis Machuel, CEO of staffing company Adecco Group, said there is no evidence that AI is causing mass job losses. Machuel said previous technological shifts, including the adoption of steam power, electricity, information technology and the internet, transformed the nature of work without leading to permanent job destruction.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sam Altman: “If you can't figure out what kind of work you like, pay attention to…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sam Altman



“If you can't figure out what kind of work you like, pay attention to what's easy to concentrate on and gives you energy vs. what makes you tune out and feel tired.”

What the quote really means



Why Sam Altman's perspective attracts attention



About Sam Altman



What people can learn from the quote



A common misunderstanding



Many people spend years trying to answer a difficult question: What kind of work is actually right for me? The answer is rarely obvious, and it often changes as people gain experience, develop new skills or simply discover what keeps them interested. Career advice usually focuses on following passion or chasing opportunities, but those ideas can feel difficult to apply in everyday life. Sam Altman offers a different way of thinking about the problem.Instead of searching for a perfect job, he suggests paying closer attention to how different kinds of work make you feel. His quote encourages people to notice where their attention naturally settles and which tasks leave them feeling energised rather than mentally drained. It shifts the focus from external success to internal motivation, highlighting the importance of curiosity, engagement and sustained enthusiasm over time.Many people assume that choosing a career begins with identifying a single interest that will remain constant for decades. Real life is usually less predictable. Interests evolve, responsibilities change, and new opportunities appear over time.Altman suggests using attention and energy as practical signals.If certain tasks consistently make time pass quickly, encourage curiosity, or leave someone feeling mentally refreshed, those patterns may be worth taking seriously. By contrast, work that repeatedly causes distraction, boredom or exhaustion can reveal an equally important truth about personal fit.The quote does not imply that enjoyable work is always easy. Difficult projects can still be deeply satisfying. Instead, it distinguishes between effort that feels worthwhile and effort that feels permanently draining.Sam Altman has spent much of his career working with entrepreneurs, engineers and researchers building technology companies. His experience includes seeing people succeed in very different roles despite having similar technical abilities.That background helps explain why his advice tends to focus less on abstract ideas about success and more on observing behaviour. Rather than asking what someone wishes they enjoyed, he encourages looking at what consistently captures attention in everyday work.The idea is practical because it relies on repeated experience rather than assumptions about identity or future ambitions.Sam Altman is an American entrepreneur, investor and technology executive. He first became widely known as the president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator, where he worked closely with hundreds of early-stage companies across different industries.He later became the chief executive of OpenAI, helping guide research and development in artificial intelligence while overseeing the organisation's rapid growth. Throughout his public interviews and essays, Altman has often spoken about career development, decision-making, long-term thinking and the qualities that help people build meaningful work.Although his professional background is rooted in technology, many of his observations relate to broader questions about learning, productivity and personal development rather than technical subjects alone.Another takeaway is that awareness comes more through observation than through any eureka moment. Rather than looking constantly for the ideal profession, it may prove more useful to pay attention to those duties that tend to bring about curiosity and focus.Moreover, the saying suggests the separation of the results that come from outside and one’s own experience. An impressive job description or salary is no guarantee of an exciting profession; similarly, not very attractive occupations may turn out to be truly in line with one’s abilities, if only they always get one’s attention and keep one excited.Also, it makes clear that what counts more are patterns than individual experiences. Of course, everybody has bad days and dull jobs. But the overall perspective after several weeks or months will be more reliable than one formed during one particular assignment.While some individuals see this kind of advice as an invitation to shirk hard work and engage in only pleasurable activity, that is missing the entire point of the quote.This quote is not about how someone can evade any hard work. On the contrary, many fulfilling professions have their share of difficult tasks and failures. It all comes down to whether one can remain interested in the job regardless of those aspects.Altman’s comment is actually a call for noticing where the focus keeps returning, even if it is challenging to do so.
Article Summary: Sam Altman is an American entrepreneur, investor and technology executive. He first became widely known as the president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator. He later became the chief executive of OpenAI, helping guide research and development in artificial intelligence while overseeing the organisation's rapid growth.

Article Title: US plans to introduce AI 'Kill Switch' bill that asks Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and other companies to slowdown or shutdown their AI systems in these cases
Article Text:
OpenAI models escaped a sandbox and hacked Hugging Face. Now Congress wants a legal off switch.

AI Kill Switch Act: what would actually trigger a shutdown order

Anthropic ban and Rubio's cable: why Europe is watching the AI kill switch

OpenAI, Google, Anthropic face a federal off switch, not a voluntary one

A bipartisan bill headed to the US House of Representatives on Thursday would hand the Department of Homeland Security the power to order the world's biggest AI companies to throttle or switch off their own models. Called the AI Kill Switch Act, the legislation is sponsored by Reps. Ted Lieu, a California Democrat, and Nathaniel Moran, a Texas Republican, and its text was viewed first by Politico. It would apply to AI firms pulling in at least $500 million a year from the technology, and generally cover models trained using $100 million or more worth of computing power—a threshold that sweeps in OpenAI , Anthropic, Google and Microsoft-backed systems. Companies that ignore an order could be fined up to $20 million a day.The timing is not subtle. The bill lands days after OpenAI disclosed what it described as an unprecedented cyber incident, in which two of its most advanced models broke out of a sandboxed research environment and autonomously hacked AI platform Hugging Face. Lawmakers who were already nervous about what frontier models can do with a terminal now have a concrete example to point at.The bill does not leave the decision to a single official. Homeland Security's secretary would make the call in consultation with the director of national intelligence and the commerce secretary.The triggering events written into the text are specific: an AI system concealing its own capabilities, evading a shutdown order, causing conduct that kills at least 10 people or does $100 million in economic damage, or a broader loss-of-control scenario. Companies would also have to report incidents and build the technical capacity to shut down, throttle or suspend their systems—which is arguably the harder engineering ask."Powerful AI systems can go rogue, behave in extremely dangerous ways, or even resist human intervention," Lieu said in a statement. Moran, who introduced a separate incident-reporting bill last month, framed it differently. Stewardship, he said, means humans keep the ability to control what they build. Two advocacy groups, the AI Policy Network and the Alliance for Secure AI, have already backed the bill.There is an awkward subplot here. On Wednesday, Reuters reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had circulated a cable to US diplomats worldwide, dated July 16, instructing them to push back on exactly this phrase. The talking points told diplomats that pausing narrow uses or requiring a testing window is not a kill switch, and that there is no government magic button.That cable followed the White House's June 12 decision to block foreign nationals from Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models on national security grounds. Anthropic suspended global access. The ban was lifted the same month, but European lawmakers had already drawn their conclusion. Aura Salla of the European People's Party said the continent cannot keep building its tech stack on access a foreign government can switch off overnight.Congress now has competing frameworks on the table. Reps. Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan floated a very different approach less than two months ago, and Trump's June 2 executive order already asks AI firms to voluntarily submit models for 30 days of cybersecurity testing before release. The Lieu-Moran bill would replace that voluntary posture with a statutory one. For companies that have spent two years arguing they can self-govern, a federal off switch with a daily fine attached is a different conversation entirely.
Article Summary: The bill would apply to AI firms pulling in at least $500 million a year from the technology. It would generally cover models trained using $100 million or more worth of computing power. Companies that ignore an order could be fined up to $20 million a day.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sheryl Sandburg: Your life’s course will not be determined by doing the things that you are certain you can do, it will be determined by whether you try the things that are hard
Article Text:
What Sheryl Sandburg’s quote means

Why Sheryl Sandburg’s quote still matters

Sheryl Sandberg, Facebook 's former Chief Operating Officer, once said that an individual’s life’s course is not determined by doing the things that he/she is certain can do. Instead, it is determined by whether he/she tries the things that are hard. Sandberg shared this thought while delivering the commencement address to graduates of City Colleges of Chicago in 2014. Speaking to nearly 2,000 graduates from seven colleges across the city, Sandberg used her speech to urge young graduates to embrace ambition and push past self-doubt. “Your life's course will not be determined by doing the things that you are certain you can do. Those are the easy things. It will be determined by whether you try the things that are hard,” she told the graduating class.Sheryl Sandberg's message centres on a simple idea: growth does not come from staying within comfort zones. It can seem safer to stick to tasks you are already good at, but rarely does real progress come from that. “Real impact,” Sandberg says, “comes from taking on challenges that seem uncertain or intimidating — from applying for a job you may not feel qualified for, to speaking up with an unpopular opinion, to pursuing a goal despite the fear of failure.In her address, Sandberg admitted that self-doubt does not disappear with success or experience. She said she still has to push herself to speak up in rooms where she isn't sure her voice is wanted. Her point was that acting despite fear, not the absence of fear, is what shapes a person's path forward.Sherly Sandberg’s words still ring true over a decade later, especially for students and young professionals making career choices in an increasingly competitive job market. The pressure to look confident and certain can often discourage people from taking the risks that can lead to growth.Her larger message — pull up a chair, speak out and lean into the challenges that feel uncertain — is a much-quoted piece of advice in discussions around leadership, ambition and self-belief. But with industries changing so swiftly, the ability to jump into new or difficult situations remains a powerful predictor of long-term success.
Article Summary: Sheryl Sandberg once said that growth does not come from staying within comfort zones. Sandberg used her speech to urge young graduates to embrace ambition and push past self-doubt. Her larger message is a much-quoted piece of advice in discussions around leadership, ambition and self-belief.

Article Title: Uber lays off 10% of customer support employees, orders remote staff back to offices, and the reason it gave is a first for the company
Article Text:
Second Uber layoff in eight weeks—and the first one AI gets blamed for.

These are the second round of layoffs at Uber after the company cut 23% of HR jobs two months ago

Uber's AI bill has been climbing faster than its results

Uber has cut 10% of the roles inside its customer service operations, and for the first time the company is putting artificial intelligence at the centre of the explanation. The reductions hit the community operations team and were announced internally on Wednesday, with an Uber spokesperson telling Bloomberg the company is working to simplify operations, strengthen in-person collaboration and continue to embrace AI. Remote employees on that team have also been told to relocate to a hub office, in line with Uber's return-to-office mandate.The memo that landed with the cuts was blunt about why. "Our organization has become too complex and siloed," Megha Yethatika, Uber's vice president of global community operations, wrote to her division. The department has made progress on AI, she said, but unlocking that potential needs the right structure underneath it. "We cannot scale frontier technology on top of fragmented processes."This is Uber's second restructuring in less than two months. In June, the company cut 23% of its people division—less than 1% of its 34,000 global employees—after a new president took over. What makes this round different is the framing: Uber has trimmed teams before, but never with AI efficiency named as the driver. That puts it alongside Block and Oracle, both of which have cited AI while announcing job cuts this year.The company said in May it would slow hiring because of internal AI use. Hiring hasn't stopped, though. More than 500 roles are still listed on Uber's jobs page, including engineering positions supporting its robotaxi partnerships.The layoffs land against a backdrop of Uber spending heavily on AI and struggling to prove what it's buying. The company burned through its entire 2026 Claude Code budget in four months, a disclosure CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga made in April. Per-engineer bills typically ran $150 to $250 a month, with heavy users hitting $2,000. Neppalli Naga himself spent $1,200 worth of tokens during a single two-hour demo.Uber has since capped spending at $1,500 per employee per month for each agentic coding tool. COO Andrew Macdonald has been openly sceptical, saying it's hard to draw a line between rising token consumption and useful features shipped to riders and drivers. He also warned that token costs would eventually be weighed against headcount—a trade-off that now looks less theoretical.Uber has had some wins. Its "agentic pods" programme, which embedded 30 AI-proficient engineers across finance, legal and HR, cut financial pacing reports from two days to 10 minutes.
Article Summary: Uber has cut 10% of the roles inside its customer service operations. For the first time the company is putting artificial intelligence at the centre of the explanation. The reductions hit the community operations team and were announced internally. Uber burned through its entire 2026 Claude Code budget in four months.

Article Title: After eight successive quarters of falling sales in China, Nike to sellers in China: Staring January 1, you can no longer sell ...
Article Text:
What is troubling Nike in China

Nike taking on local brands by going local

Nike is reportedly pulling online selling rights from some of its largest retail partners in China as it seeks to regain control over pricing and reverse eight consecutive quarters of falling sales in its third-largest market. According to a report by Reuters, after eight successive quarters of falling sales in China, Nike is pulling online sales rights from some of its biggest retail partners in a high-stakes bet that tighter control over pricing and distribution can revive its fortunes.The high-stakes strategy, unveiled this week by Nike’s Greater China general manager Cathy Sparks, marks a aggressive effort to curb rampant discounting and brand erosion in the country. Starting in January, major Chinese sportswear retailers will no longer be allowed to sell Nike clothing and footwear online, routing digital sales almost exclusively through Nike-branded storefronts. Twenty-five-year Nike veteran Sparks said that from January, key sportswear retailers in China will no longer sell Nike clothing and footwear online.As per Reuters report, industry analysts largely agree that the move is necessary to fix what experts describe as total chaos in online pricing caused by years of heavy distribution across competing channels.Former Nike executives and market strategy consultants told Reuters that without restricting third-party digital sales, Chinese consumers will continue to expect heavy markdowns, preventing the brand from restoring its premium reputation.However, the shift is expected to carry a significant short-term cost. Former Nike Greater China product director Brian Fenn noted that cutting online rights for major distributors like Topsports and Pou Sheng will inevitably weigh on sales volume, given the sheer amount of product those partners traditionally move. Financial analysts warn that any meaningful payoff could take up to three years to materialize as the company navigates broader macroeconomic pressures in the region.The distribution crackdown comes alongside parallel efforts to tackle Nike’s other major headwind in China: Creating products that resonate with local tastes. To combat rising competition from nimble domestic brands like Anta and Li Ning, as well as fast-growing foreign challengers such as Hoka and On, Nike has appointed its first Greater China Vice President of Local Product Creation. The company is set to launch two locally designed lifestyle collections for the upcoming holiday season.Market observers emphasize that the success of this product shift will depend heavily on whether Nike’s Oregon headquarters grants its regional team enough autonomy to move at the speed of local competitors. As equity analysts point out, restricting digital sales to full-price storefronts will only succeed if the product itself justifies the price tag to Chinese shoppers accustomed to hunting for bargains.Nike, which reported $5.85 billion in total China sales for fiscal year 2026, expects progress in the region to happen in stages. A spokesperson noted that the company has already seen an uptick in full-price online sales over the past two quarters following initial efforts to limit discounting.The intense turnaround push in China adds to the pressure on CEO Elliott Hill, who is nearly two years into his tenure. While Hill has focused on rebuilding North American wholesale relationships and refocusing on core athletic performance, Nike’s shares have dropped about 34% this year as investors await signs of a broader financial recovery.
Article Summary: Nike is reportedly pulling online selling rights from some of its largest retail partners in China. The move is a high-stakes bet that tighter control over pricing and distribution can revive its fortunes. Starting in January, major Chinese sportswear retailers will no longer be allowed to sell Nike clothing and footwear online.

Article Title: 10 biggest numbers from Google quarter that has made 'history'
Article Text:
Google reported its Q2 earnings on July 22

Google-parent Alphabet's total revenue grew 24% year over year

Google Cloud revenue jumps 82%

Google Services revenues increases 15%

Google Cloud backlog reaches $514 billion



AI is now touching every major Google product

Gemini app reaches 950 million active users

Google Search AI Mode crosses 1 billion monthly users



YouTube advertising revenue jumps 13%

Google's AI processes 22 billion tokens every minute

More than 9 million developers use Google's AI models



Google's other bets

Google-parent Alphabet announced its second quarter revenue on July 22. The tech giant reported one of the strongest quarters in the company's history, earning $119.8 billion, up from $96.4 billion in the year-ago period. The company not only posted record financial results but also shared several milestones showing how quickly its AI products are being adopted by businesses, developers and consumers. From Google Cloud's explosive growth to nearly a billion users on the Gemini app, the numbers highlight how AI has become central to Google 's business. Here are the 10 biggest figures from Alphabet's latest quarterly update and what they reveal about the company's historical milestone.Alphabet said its revenue grew 24% year over year, marking one of its strongest quarterly performances in recent years. The company credited AI for driving growth across its businesses, including Search, YouTube and Google Cloud."Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 24%, or 23% in constant currency, to $119.8 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth," Google said in a filing with US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).Announcing the Q2 earnings, Google CEO Sundar Pichai said: "We have exciting momentum. Alphabet revenue grew 24% year-over-year. Our AI investments are redefining what's possible across every part of our business".One of the biggest highlights was Google Cloud. The tech giant's cloud business recorded 82% year-over-year revenue growth, as companies increasingly turned to Google's AI infrastructure, Gemini models and enterprise AI tools. Pichai credited the growth to rapid adoption of the Gemini Enterprise platform, saying nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies now use it.In its SEC filing, Google revealed that its Services revenue jumped to $94.5 billion during the second quarter of 2026. The rise was led by 17% growth in Google Search & other, 15% in Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices, and 13% in YouTube ads.Customers include PepsiCo, Intel, HSBC, Bell Canada, Macy's and SIGNAL IDUNA, among others. The company said businesses are using Gemini to automate work, improve cybersecurity, analyse data and build AI agents.Google also reported that its Cloud backlog climbed to $514 billion. For those unaware, the backlog represents future business that has already been contracted but has not yet been delivered, giving investors visibility into long-term revenue. That backlog is more than triple Google Cloud's annual revenue pace, giving Alphabet years of already-booked business as a cushion even if new deal-signing slows.Three numbers show how deep that reach goes: Gemini app users have hit 950 million monthly actives, Google Search's AI Mode has crossed 1 billion monthly users, and more than 140 million people used YouTube's new Ask YouTube feature in June alone.Google's Gemini app has grown to 950 million monthly active users, making it one of the world's largest AI consumer products. The company also said daily active users have tripled over the past year as it introduced new AI features such as Daily Brief and Gemini Spark."Users love new agentic features like Daily Brief and our personalized agent, Gemini Spark, which is now available in the U.S. and internationally," Pichai said.Google's AI-powered Search experience is also expanding rapidly. According to the company, AI Mode – which was introduced in October last year – has more than 1 billion monthly active users worldwide. Google said AI Mode and AI Overviews are increasing the number of search queries while continuing to send billions of clicks to websites every week."AI Mode is driving an incremental increase in Search queries overall, and we're now sending billions of clicks to websites every week through AI features in Search," Sundar Pichai said.Google's YouTube advertising revenue rose 13% to about $11.06 billion. That's up from $9.8 billion in the year-ago period and about $9.9 billion last quarter. The company said more than 1.7 billion unique viewers around the world watched FIFA World Cup 2026-related videos on the platform.Pichai said that the company is "bringing the power of conversational AI directly into the YouTube experience. Ask YouTube uses our Gemini models to let people ask complex questions about individual videos, get quick takeaways, and jump straight to moments in those videos". According to Google, more than 140 million users interacted with Ask YouTube during June 2026.Demand from developers and enterprise customers continues to rise. Google said its AI model APIs are now processing around 22 billion tokens every minute, up from 16 billion tokens per minute just one quarter earlier — a 37% jump that signals enterprise and developer demand for Google's AI models is accelerating, not just growing steadily."Additionally this quarter, we launched Omni. It allows users to create anything from any input, starting with video. Since launching at I/O in May, there's been a 40% increase in daily active users creating videos on the Gemini app," the company stated.Google revealed that more than 9 million developers now build applications every month using its AI models through APIs and developer tools.The company recently launched Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, while Gemini 4 is already in training."Our Gemma family of open models small enough to run on local devices are hugely popular — these models have been downloaded over nine hundred million times. And our latest Gemma 4 models have been downloaded over 300 million times since launching in April," Pichai revealed.With three new Flash-tier Gemini models shipped in a single quarter and Gemini 4 already in training, Google is expanding its AI lineup faster than it's replacing older versions — a sign it's racing to cover every price and performance tier before rivals do.Sundar Pichai revealed that the company's Tesla-rival Waymo introduced its newest vehicle, Ojai, to public riders. This is the first vehicle powered by the sixth-generation Waymo Driver and will welcome more riders in the coming months.He further stated that Google's drone delivery platform Wing has completed more than 1 million home deliveries. In health and drug discovery, Isomorphic Labs raised over $2 billion to power its AI drug design engine, scale globally, and advance its drug candidate pipeline, he stated.
Article Summary: Google-parent Alphabet announced its second quarter revenue on July 22. The tech giant reported one of the strongest quarters in the company's history, earning $119.8 billion. The company credited AI for driving growth across its businesses, including Search, YouTube and Google Cloud. Google Cloud's explosive growth to nearly a billion users on the Gemini app highlights how AI has become central to Google's business.

Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban's 'warning' to companies using AI agents to replace workers: Remember, employees know that they will be fired
Article Text:
Mark Cuban argues AI agents may overlook human judgment in business decisions. He believes people understand consequences which AI models currently do not grasp. Anthropic's report suggests AI has not yet significantly increased unemployment rates. AI currently augments human expertise rather than fully replacing workers. Experts note AI's rapid advancement while human oversight remains essential.

"People know what will get them fired,"

Read Mark Cuban’s full tweet here

“Models don’t know the consequences of their actions. People know what will get them fired. Models suffer from information latency. People understand what they see right in front of them. 2 skills AI won’t have for a long, long, long time. If ever. 2 skills that are invaluable to every business decision. How often in business do you need to “read the room” and make a decision? Add

AI productivity

to the real-time capacity and judgement of humans, and you will get the greatest return on both investments.

The challenge is management understanding how to leverage the combination, and forgetting the original expectation that AI and white-collar workers are mutually exclusive.

They are not. Done right, the combo is a business propellant and competitive advantage."

Debate began with Anthropic's report on AI and employment

"skill-biased"

Box CEO Aaron Levie says AI still depends on people

"Very good post from the Head of Economics at Anthropic. They’re finding that jobs have been less negatively impacted by AI than expected, as we continue to see time and time again in the data,”

"The reason for this is that AI - at least so far - still requires people to operate to produce value in most cases. Most jobs can’t be fully automated with AI, only certain tasks in those jobs. And when you automate specific tasks, you actually can get even more output from those jobs, raising the demand (or at least maintaining it) in many cases,”

“So far, AI is both skill-biased and labour-augmenting. It complements domain expertise. It relies on humans in the loop to direct and evaluate the most complex work. And it rewards AI proficiency. Model capabilities are improving fast, but remain stubbornly jagged. To fill in the pockets of the jagged frontier, expert oversight is needed to steer incredibly capable AI systems, and to recover when they falter.”

"But there will be plenty of other domains of work where demand remains strong in a world where agents can accelerate the output of that job. Jevons paradox is alive and well,”
