Anthropic's report suggests AI has not yet significantly increased unemployment rates. AI currently augments human expertise rather than fully replacing workers.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai reminder to analysts: Yes we may need to improve in AI Coding and Agentic Coding, but there are areas in AI we clearly lead
Article Text:
Google CEO Sundar Pichai

Sundar Pichai teases Gemini 4 release



Google-parent Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai mounted a robust defense of Google's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy during the company's earnings call on Wednesday, July 22, pushing back against investor fears that the search giant is trailing rivals following flagship model delays and setbacks in AI coding. Investor anxiety has reportedly mounted over Google’s decision to postpone Gemini 3.5 Pro, a model initially scheduled for a June release aimed at strengthening Google's foothold in AI coding and autonomous agents. The delay has heightened concerns that Google is losing momentum while competitors like OpenAI, Anthropic, and several Chinese rivals rapidly launch new models.Addressing analysts on Q2 earnings call, Pichai adopted an unusually defensive posture when pressed on whether Google's frontier models could continue to compete at the industry's cutting edge. "We've had clearly frontier models. There are many attributes on which we are still at the frontier; there are areas where we've acknowledged we need to improve and coding and agentic coding is an example of that," Pichai said in response to JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth, according to a Reuters report.Rather than focusing on the delayed flagship model, Pichai directed attention toward Gemini Flash, Google's lower-cost "workhorse" model designed to power enterprise applications, data analytics, and customer service.He highlighted the newly released Gemini 3.6 Flash, noting significant performance gains on coding benchmarks alongside newly unveiled variants like Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Flash Cyber, while Gemini 3.5 Pro remains in partner testing.Looking ahead, Pichai teased the upcoming Gemini 4 release, describing it as a "very ambitious effort" trained on a substantially larger scale. He told Barclays analyst Ross Sandler that Google's roadmap for Gemini 4 includes rolling out models "almost at a monthly cadence," reiterating that the company remains "very committed and very confident" in maintaining its edge.Despite reporting a stark 82% surge in cloud growth -- surpassing Wall Street estimates of 64% -- Alphabet’s capital expenditures continue to draw scrutiny. The company raised its capex guidance by $15 billion to a range between $195 billion and $205 billion.Google is the first of the Big Tech companies to report quarterly results. Meta Platforms, Microsoft and Amazon follow next week.
Article Summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai defends company's AI strategy on Q2 earnings call. Investor anxiety has reportedly mounted over Google’s decision to postpone Gemini 3.5 Pro, a model aimed at strengthening Google's foothold in AI coding and autonomous agents.

Article Title: Nvidia gifts its supercomputer to US military university, donation is first direct use of the company's top-end servers by American military; here's what CEO Jensen Huang said
Article Text:
About DGX GB300 that Nvidia donated to US military university

Nvidia has donated a supercomputer, Nvidia DGX GB300 system with its latest chips, to a nonprofit linked to US military university – Naval Postgraduate School (NPS). The donation marks the first direct use of Nvidia's most advanced servers by the US military. “Our nation depends on our men and women who fight on the front lines. Nothing is more valuable to you than information and insight, and information and insight in a timely way, and to understand its impact and consequence,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said announcing the gift. “I can’t imagine anything more important,” he further added.Huang, who visited Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey, California told the attendees: “Leadership is about being in service of something else. You’re in service of your team. You’re in service of your country. You’re in service of your mission. And all of this technology is just tools to help you”.In a blog post, Nvidia said that the DGX GB300 supercomputer is equipped with Nvidia Mission Control software that gives NPS’s more than 1,500 in-resident students and 600 faculty on-premises access to large-scale AI computing, including model training and inference capability for applications spanning weather prediction, cybersecurity, and disaster resilience and response planning.It’s built based on an Nvidia AI Technology Center on the Monterey campus — a dedicated hub for AI research and graduate instruction, now anchored by the DGX GB300.“As we modernize our technology, we must also modernize how we educate our leaders,” said Admiral Samuel Paparo, commander of the U.S. Pacific Command. “Access to advanced computing capability means NPS students and faculty understand the opportunities and responsibilities that come with these technologies.”Nvidia has partnered with DDN, VAST and Vertiv for hardware and systems integration. DDN, the company said, contributed high-performance data infrastructure to help researchers efficiently access, manage, protect and scale data for demanding AI workloads.VAST Data provided a unified data platform to enable secure data access and management across edge, core and cloud environments. Vertiv provided the racks, cooling and power infrastructure needed to bring the system online, as well as installation sequencing, testing and commissioning support, and fluid management and monitoring.
Article Summary: Nvidia has donated a supercomputer, Nvidia DGX GB300 system with its latest chips, to a nonprofit linked to US military university – Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) The donation marks the first direct use of Nvidia's most advanced servers by the US military.

Portage College of Calgary, Canada has asked Indian students protesting after their work visa got rejected by the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to seek legal advice, stating that it “continues to seek clarification regarding this issue”. In an update shared on the website dated July 21, the college said: “Portage College continues to seek clarification regarding this issue and remains committed to providing factual information and keeping students informed as new information becomes available”. The college further revealed that it has scheduled a follow-up meeting with representatives from the group next week. “This meeting will provide an opportunity to continue our dialogue, answer questions where we are able, and share any new information that becomes available,” it added.Thousands of Indian students attended the Portage College’s business management diploma program. After completing their program, the students applied for post graduate work permitS (PGWP). But the IRCC rejected their applications stating their programs were not eligible.The protesting students argue that others from the same college and the same programs have received PGWP approvals before July 7. They further allege that the immigration authority has changed a rule and made non-credit programs ineligible for the permit.IRCC, on its part, claim that no rule change has been done.On the website, the Portage College has advised students to retain important documents that may be relevant to any future application, request for reconsideration, or other process undertaken on the advice of an authorized immigration professional. List of documents that students should keep copies of include:• Study permits• Letters of acceptance• Enrolment records• Program completion documents• Transcripts• PGWP applications• IRCC refusal letters and officer notes, if available• Correspondence with IRCC or an authorized immigration representativePortage college has also published FAQs addressing concerns of Indian students. Addressing one such query, the college said that it can not overturn the IRCC decision, adding “IRCC has sole authority over immigration decisions. Any student who wishes to pursue a legal or immigration process must do so independently or through an authorized representative.Students should consult the current Government of Canada and IRCC materials regarding PGWP eligibility and requirements. Because immigration rules and guidance may change, students should rely on the current official information and obtain independent advice about their individual circumstances.211 Alberta: https://ab.211.ca/

Article Title: US government just told Harvard, Stanford, MIT and other top universities that more than you individual scientists can 'help' America beat China
Article Text:
What this may mean for Harvard, Stanford, MIT and other US universities

4 key recommendations made in the federal report

Revitalize America’s Science and Technology Enterprise

Secure U.S. Dominance in Critical and Emerging Technologies

Launch a New Golden Age Powered by AI for Science

Ensure That Science and Technology Better the Lives of All Americans

The US government plans to give money to individual scientists directly, instead of large universities and established institutions like Harvard, Stanford and MIT for science and research, especially in the AI era. The Trump administration has sent a memo to federal departments and agencies, outlining the roadmap to revitalize American research and development (R&D). According to a White House press release, the overhaul plan was laid out in a report titled ‘Science: A New Golden Age’ published by Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Michael Kratsios. The directives will help shape a roughly $200 billion annual federal research and development budget across the government for the rest of President Donald Trump’s second term.In both report and memo, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy argues that individual scientists can accelerate technological discovery to defeat China. “American scientific progress was the beating heart of the 20th century. After World War II, we adapted to a new world by reinventing our scientific institutions, and we must do so again today. This report lays a policy foundation that frees American scientists to do their most groundbreaking work, revives the national pursuit of ambitious scientific missions, and positions the United States to lead the AI-driven scientific revolution that will define the next century,” said Director Kratsios.The Trump administration said it wants to give more support to programs that fund individual researchers instead of colleges and universities. The report further points to programs such as the National Science Foundation's graduate fellowships and the National Institutes of Health's awards for innovative scientists as examples to follow. It also says that some universities could face challenges under a proposed Office of Management and Budget rule. The proposal would give political appointees more control over research grants and make sure funding matches the administration's priorities.As per a Wall Street Journal report, the new guidance may hurt large universities that rely on federal research funding.The White House has given federal R&D agencies “to submit an action plan within 90 days outlining implementation of these priority practices, while incorporating the budget guidance into their FY2028 submissions to the Office of Management and Budget”.The report organizes its recommendations to government, industry, academia, and philanthropy around four key pillars:The R&D enterprise should refocus support on individual scientists rather than legacy institutions, diversify funding mechanisms beyond slow consensus peer review, create agile new research organizations such as X-Labs and expanded ARPA-like entities, and establish metascience units to institutionalize continuous improvement.Federal R&D should prioritize national mission-driven scientific initiatives that unite government, industry, academia, and philanthropy around ambitious goals. These include the Genesis Mission to double the productivity of American research through AI; the Quantum Computer for Application Development and Discovery Science (QC-ADDS); commercial fusion power demonstration by the mid-2030s; crewed lunar return and lunar base development; and next-generation semiconductor technologies.The Federal government should fully fund and scale the Genesis Mission as the flagship national AI-for-science initiative to dramatically accelerate discovery; develop domain-specific scientific foundation models and high-value datasets, invest in AI-enabled verification infrastructure and autonomous laboratories; and begin transitioning toward AI-native scientific institutions better suited to an era of machine-augmented research.Federal agencies should integrate hands-on technical training and apprenticeships into STEM education, open scientific careers to skilled craftspeople and practitioners, build dense regional innovation clusters that link research with advanced manufacturing, and ensure that the economic returns of discovery reach every region and community in the country.
Article Summary: The US government plans to give money to individual scientists directly, instead of large universities and established institutions like Harvard, Stanford and MIT. The Trump administration has sent a memo to federal departments and agencies, outlining the roadmap to revitalize American research and development (R&D) The report organizes its recommendations to government, industry, academia, and philanthropy around four key pillars.

Article Title: Google made history on July 22, with more profit in three months than 459 of the Fortune 500 companies generate in top line revenue in a full year
Article Text:
Google booked $99 billion in “other income”

Google-parent Alphabet has become the first company in the world to report more than $100 billion in quarterly profit, setting a new corporate record. In its second-quarter earnings released on July 22, the company posted a net income of $112.1 billion, nearly four times higher than a year ago. According to Fortune, the figure is more profit in three months than 459 Fortune 500 companies generate in total annual revenue. Helped by an 82% jump in Google Cloud revenue, Alphabet’s revenue rose 24% year over year to $119.8 billion. The record earnings were also driven by massive gains from the company's investments in artificial intelligence firm Anthropic and Elon Musk’s SpaceX.Google CEO Sundar Pichai said the results show that the company's "full stack approach to AI is delivering real, measurable value."A footnote in Alphabet’s Q2 earnings release revealed that a large part of the record profit came from $99 billion in "other income", which included “unrealized and realized gains” from Alphabet's investment portfolio. According to the company's earnings release, these gains added $77.1 billion to its net income after taxes.Much of these investment gain came from Alphabet's stakes in Claude-maker Anthropic and Elon Musk-owned space company SpaceX, both of which saw their valuations rise sharply during the quarter.Alphabet has invested $300 million in Anthropic in 2023, and that investment has since grown significantly. The companies also have a cloud partnership under which Anthropic has agreed to buy large amounts of computing capacity from Google Cloud, supporting the cloud business's rapid growth.Similarly, Alphabet owns a roughly 6% stake in SpaceX that went public last month at a valuation of $1.77 trillion. These paper gains helped bolster Alphabet’s investment portfolio and flowed through to its bottom line.Despite the record earnings, Alphabet shares fell about 3% in after-hours trading. Investors remained concerned about the company's rising spending on AI infrastructure and increasing competition for its Gemini family of AI models.
Article Summary: Alphabet posted a net income of $112.1 billion, nearly four times higher than a year ago. The figure is more profit in three months than 459 Fortune 500 companies generate in total annual revenue. The record earnings were driven by massive gains from the company's investments in artificial intelligence firm Anthropic and Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

Article Title: US government accuses Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI of 'stealing' Anthropic's Fable model; says covert distillation to steal US technology is "unacceptable"
Article Text:
Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable model, says White House official Michael Kratsios



Kimi K3 is a 2.8 trillion-parameter open-weight model that beat US benchmarks



US sanctions on Chinese AI models are now on the table, says Scott Bessent



The White House has accused Chinese startup Moonshot AI of stealing from Anthropic to build Kimi K3, the open-weight model that knocked tech stocks around last week. Michael Kratsios, who runs the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, posted on X on Wednesday that the US government has information showing Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Fable model to create K3. The more damning part of his claim is what came next: Moonshot allegedly built an internal platform specifically to run this at scale, one that could switch between different ways of accessing US models so the activity stayed invisible.Kratsios stacked a second charge on top. He said Moonshot acquired servers fitted with Nvidia GB300 chips and used them in Thailand, likely for training. Those chips belong to the Blackwell generation, which Washington does not allow Chinese firms to buy anywhere in the world. Both accusations arrived a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went on Fox Business and said the US could sanction Chinese companies for what he called, without much hedging, theft. Moonshot has said nothing. Neither has the Chinese embassy in Washington.Distillation means training a smaller model on the outputs of a bigger one. It is ordinary practice, and Kratsios said so himself, calling legitimate distillation a vital part of the open innovation ecosystem.What he objects to is the scale and the concealment. His words: large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary US technology and undermining American research is unacceptable.Anthropic has been making this case for months. In February it named Moonshot alongside DeepSeek and MiniMax, alleging Moonshot ran hundreds of fake accounts through roughly 3.4 million exchanges with Claude. In June it accused Alibaba of the largest distillation attack it had recorded. Sarah Heck, Anthropic's head of public policy, thanked Kratsios on X and framed the practice as industrial espionage that ends up feeding foreign military and intelligence capability.Moonshot showed K3 last week and called it the largest open-weight system in the world at 2.8 trillion parameters. On coding and general capability benchmarks it sits level with or above Anthropic and OpenAI's frontier models. By Moonshot's own accounting, only Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 come out ahead overall. The full weights go up on July 27, free to download and modify, which is the part that actually worries American labs. Anthropic and OpenAI spent billions getting to this point. Moonshot is giving its version away.The timeline is also why the distillation claim has drawn scepticism. Fable came out about a week before K3, and Kratsios produced no evidence.Bessent said the administration is finding watermarks from American models showing up in Chinese ones. He supports open source, he said, but open source is not open season on American IP. Axios has reported the White House is weighing a rule that would let US companies host Chinese models only if they guarantee security and accept liability for breaches, and that similar efforts were killed internally last year before national security hawks regained ground.The pushback is coming from inside the industry. Chamath Palihapitiya called it a China boogeyman used to protect the equity of a few thousand investors. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue was blunter: if distillation were the whole story, plenty of other countries would already have great open models. China's research teams, he said, are simply better and more open than America's.
Article Summary: White House official Michael Kratsios says Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Fable model to create Kimi K3. He also claims Moonshot acquired servers fitted with Nvidia GB300 chips and used them in Thailand, likely for training. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US could sanction Chinese companies for what he called, without much hedging, theft.

Article Text:

Multimodal Screen Reasoning wherein Gemini can read what’s on your screen to execute requests, such as converting a photo of a handwritten grocery list into an online order.



Background Execution where users can track Gemini's step-by-step progress, jump in to adjust details, or close the phone and let the AI run in the background. Gemini alerts the user when the task is ready for final review.



Gemini Notebook now comes preinstalled on new Samsung foldables



Hands-free AI for watches and smart glasses

Samsung has launched the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, and Z Flip8 smartphones at the Galaxy Unpacked in London. At the event, Google showcased a deeply integrated suite of artificial intelligence (AI) features powering Samsung’s newest flagship devices. Leading the showcase is Gemini Intelligence, Google’s next-generation AI designed to handle complex everyday tasks proactively. Google outlined three major updates coming to the Samsung ecosystem.Building on a task automation beta launched earlier this year, Gemini can now handle routine “life admin” across more than 40 popular apps. Users can delegate tasks such as booking travel experiences, buying event tickets, making dinner reservations and ordering rideshares directly through the assistant. On the Galaxy Z Flip8, users can trigger task automation straight from the outer Flex Window by long-pressing the power button.The key upgrades powering these features include:To help users organize complex projects, Google is bringing Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) directly to Samsung's foldable lineup as a preinstalled app. It has been optimised for the larger inner screens of the Galaxy Z Fold8 series.Every new Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8 purchase includes a six-month trial of Google AI Pro, granting access to advanced multimodal features like Audio and Video Overviews.Google and Samsung are also taking Gemini beyond smartphones. On Galaxy Watch 9, users can activate Gemini by raising their wrist—no wake word required. Samsung launched Samsung smart glasses partnership with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, and these wearables can be controlled via Wear OS wrist gestures.At the event, Google unveiled two additional frame designs for its smart glasses lineup, confirming that users wearing a compatible Wear OS smartwatch will be able to navigate their glasses using simple hand gestures.

Article Title: Scientists found millions of fish nests stretching across the seafloor like a vast city, how underwater robot 'Lassie' helped in the discovery beneath the ice of Antarctica’s Weddell Sea
Article Text:
Representative Image

"Lassie,"

"Lassie"

How the iceberg exposed the hidden ecosystem

"Lassie"

Yellowfin notie fish build and guard the nests

"selfish herd"

Expedition also searched for Shackleton's Endurance

Findings could support conservation efforts

Scientists have uncovered a hidden fish breeding ground in Antarctica. The discovery was made beneath the ice of Antarctica's Weddell Sea after the A68 iceberg broke away from the Larsen C Ice Shelf in 2017. This incident exposed the seabed that had been covered by around 200 metres of ice. Using underwater robots, including the remotely operated vehicle (ROV)researchers documented thousands of organised fish nests, adding to evidence of a much larger breeding habitat stretching across the seafloor.The discovery was made during the 2019 Weddell Sea Expedition, which employed autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and the remotely operated vehicleto explore the newly accessible area. The researchers found more than 1,000 circular nests in organised formations, each cleared of plankton debris covering the surrounding seabed. The findings support previous studies that indicate the area is one of the largest known fish breeding colonies in the world.The opportunity to study the region arose after the A68 iceberg, which covered about 5,800 square kilometres, calved from the Larsen C Ice Shelf in 2017. The event opened access to a section of the seafloor that had previously remained hidden beneath the ice shelf.Scientists aboard the South African polar research vessel SA Agulhas II used AUVs and the ROVto survey the seabed. Images captured by the underwater vehicles showed circular nests arranged in geometric clusters rather than randomly scattered across the seafloor.Each nest had been cleared of phytoplankton detritus, suggesting active maintenance by the fish.Researchers identified the nest builders as yellowfin notie (Lindbergichthys nudifrons), a species of Antarctic rockcod. Each nest is guarded by an adult fish that protects its eggs from predators.According to the expedition, the nesting pattern may reflect thetheory, in which fish nesting near the centre of the colony gain additional protection from predators. At the same time, larger individuals occupy nests along the edges, where defence is more challenging.The 2019 Weddell Sea Expedition had two objectives: conducting scientific research near the Larsen C Ice Shelf and searching for Sir Ernest Shackleton's ship, Endurance, which sank in 1915.Although heavy sea ice prevented the team from locating the wreck during the expedition, the experience gained from operating underwater vehicles in difficult conditions contributed to the Endurance22 mission, which located the wreck in March 2022 at a depth of 3,008 metres.Scientists say the nesting grounds provide further evidence that the region contains a Vulnerable Marine Ecosystem that supports Antarctic biodiversity. The findings also expand on work published by Purser and colleagues in 2022 that found one of the largest known fish breeding colonies on Earth in the Weddell Sea.Researchers say documenting these underwater habitats could help proposals to make the Weddell Sea a Marine Protected Area, conserving breeding grounds that are part of Antarctica’s marine ecosystem.
Article Summary: Discovery was made beneath the ice of Antarctica's Weddell Sea after the A68 iceberg broke away from the Larsen C Ice Shelf in 2017. This incident exposed the seabed that had been covered by around 200 metres of ice. Using underwater robots, scientists documented thousands of organised fish nests, adding to evidence of a much larger breeding habitat stretching across the seafloor.

Article Title: Eternal plays down Toing, Ownly threat in battle for cheaper meals
Article Text: Bengaluru: Zomato parent company Eternal on Wednesday played down the early traction of newer food-delivery platforms Swiggy-owned Toing and Rapido-owned Ownly, saying their appeal is being driven largely by discounts rather than a genuinely new consumer proposition.The comments come as food-delivery companies sharpen their focus on meals priced around Rs 200, a market aimed at officegoers and other value-conscious customers. As TOI reported last week, platforms are experimenting with lower menu prices, reduced commissions and cheaper delivery to make ordering food a more regular habit.Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal argued that the newer apps had not created a materially different service. They largely list the same restaurants and are not faster, he said, while their lower menu prices are being subsidised through reduced commissions and delivery charges.“There’s no new use case being unlocked here,” Goyal said in the company’s shareholder letter. “The customer traction is purely price-driven, and price-driven traction without structural economics tends to resolve itself.”Eternal has, however, responded selectively where rivals are spending more aggressively.On the analyst call, chief financial officer Akshant Goyal said Zomato had remained price-competitive in such markets and had so far been able to defend its share.One measure taken earlier was to lower the minimum order eligible for free delivery for Zomato Gold members to Rs 99 from Rs 199. This made smaller food orders more affordable without requiring the company to launch a separate value-focused app.Management said it was not spending much energy tracking the newer platforms. Instead, Eternal is betting on Bistro, its own low-priced meal experiment, which uses specialised kitchens, limited menus and custom equipment to serve food in the Rs 50-150 range.Bistro is expanding cautiously, adding roughly 10 kitchens a quarter. Eternal said throughput at some older kitchens was improving as it refined menus, pricing and operations. Expansion could accelerate once the model becomes more predictable.For now, Zomato’s core food-delivery business continues to grow. Its net order value rose more than 20% to Rs 10,769 crore in the June quarter, marking a fourth straight quarter of acceleration. Adjusted operating profit increased 34% to Rs 606 crore.
Article Summary: Zomato parent company Eternal played down the early traction of newer food- delivery platforms Swiggy-owned Toing and Rapido-owned Ownly. Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal argued that the newer apps had not created a materially different service.
